status: EMPTY, DELIBERATELY (D197). The machinery ships; the inventory does not. Writing an ad here means printing a real company's name on a card nobody bought — D1's no-fabrication rule pointed at a claim about money rather than about a crowd, and the worse of the two: an invented crowd misleads about a number, an invented advertiser misleads about a relationship. The first row arrives with a contract behind it.
comment: Feed ads (docs/MONETIZATION.md path 3). AN AD IS NOT A SPONSORED QUESTION, and the two are kept apart on purpose — path 2 sells a QUESTION, which is answered like any other and folds into the same public aggregate everyone reads; path 3 sells a CARD, which takes no answer and produces no data at all. They share the disclosure band and the single paid slot; they are otherwise different objects, and prose that blurs them makes the disclosure argument impossible to have (D196).
authoring: Five rules, and `npm run check:content` holds all five:
1. TEXT ONLY. `advertiser`, `headline`, `body` — and nothing else.
No image, no logo, no brand colour, no link. Every one of those is
refused by name rather than by omission, so adding one is a
conversation rather than a commit.
2. NO TAP-THROUGH. There is nowhere for the card to send you, which is
why there is nothing to count. This is what keeps the ad path free
of the measurement apparatus MONETIZATION.md rules out: with no
click there is no click to attribute, and billing stays on the
answers the sponsored-question path already publishes.
3. A WINDOW. `until` is a UTC day key, the same field and the same
filter the feed already uses to stop serving an expired card.
4. AT MOST ONE AUDIENCE TAG, from the published breakdown dims, matched
ON THE DEVICE (src/v2/data/sponsored.ts). The server is never asked
who should see what.
5. THE BAND IS THE APP'S. The disclosure is drawn by ui/SponsorMark
— the app's ink, the word PAID, the advertiser's name, the window —
and an advertiser cannot restyle it, because nothing in this file
can carry a style.
Ads are never questions, so they carry no options, no provenance row
and no aggregate. They are seeded to v2_ads, which is read-only to
every client and written only by the seed.
